result.summary:
Scope test: YES, real application-executable surface (React component + API client + regression/e2e tests). Read lib/letflow/design/req383-appearance-settings-screen.md in full, then independently re-verified each of REQ-383's 5 acceptance criteria against the actual test assertions in web/src/components/ui/__tests__/StatusBadge.test.tsx and web/tests/e2e/pipelines/tenant-branding.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts, plus a direct read of AppearanceSettingsPage.tsx and a grep of tenant-branding-applied.yaml for the NOTE removal.

Finding: NO GAP. Every criterion is already covered by a real, failing-if-violated test:
- AC1 (submit + round-trip + confirmation, immediate effect no reload): e2e test 1 asserts the confirmation banner appears AND reads the live --color-brand-600 custom property to prove the new colour took effect, explicitly without ever calling page.reload() -- the correct proof for 'no full reload required'.
- AC2 (contrast-refused: plain-language message, previous colour stays): e2e test 2 asserts the error banner is non-empty, matches WCAG/contrast wording, does NOT match Ecto/changeset-blob patterns, AND that the live colour is unchanged from baseline -- closes the exact client.ts details.detail-vs-message footgun the design doc's own S0 flagged.
- AC3 (StatusBadge colours unaffected): 4 unit tests (TC-REQ383-01..04) capture StatusBadge's resolved inline styles before/after a REAL (unmocked) applyBrandingColors() call and assert byte-for-byte identity, plus an explicit never-equals-var(--color-brand-600) check -- a genuine regression test, not a restated code-reading claim.
- AC4 (no out-of-scope-key path): verified by construction/enumeration by reading the finished AppearanceSettingsPage.tsx directly -- exactly one form control, one state variable, one mutation call site, one literal request-body object with two hardcoded keys, no spread/dynamic-key/escape-hatch anywhere. This matches AC4's OWN acceptance-criteria text, which specifies this verification method explicitly ('stated and verified explicitly... not by testing a server-side reject path a same-origin form can never trigger') -- a runnable test here would be testing REQ-382's server-side logic (already covered by tenant_settings_test.exs's AC3), not this screen, so none was written.
- AC5 (stale NOTE removed, e2e spec exists/passes with screenshot pair): grepped tenant-branding-applied.yaml -- zero ISS-0527 matches, pipeline_test: still names the now-real spec file. e2e test 3 (EO-005) captures the required first-paint/settled-frame screenshot pair and asserts the flash's polarity as a documented-not-fixed regression pin.

Wrote test/specs/REQ-383.md mapping all 5 acceptance criteria to their existing test cases with why-each-exists rationale (matching the established test/specs/REQ-382.md convention). No new test code was written -- inventing a duplicate or trivially-different test against already-correct code would be exactly the manufactured-busywork anti-pattern this role is forbidden from producing, and FRONTEND-DEV's own gate run (quoted in step-02b-frontend-dev.json: type-check exit 0, lint exit 0, 801/801 tests passed, guards 48/48 passed) already covers these files -- TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 re-runs the full suite independently regardless.

No wall-clock/unseeded-randomness dependency in any of the reviewed tests (e2e fixture colours are hardcoded hex literals matching the backend's own WCAG test fixtures, not derived at runtime; EO-005's poll has a fixed timeout, not a sleep).
